text:
Aisha: :rotating_light: FYI customers in EU reported increased 5xxs and timeouts starting ~09:12 UTC. Looks like region routing picked the wrong endpoint and traffic went to us-central instead of europe-west1.
Tom: Got the complaints — some apps show long client-side latency (300-700ms extra) and a handful of 401s. Support stacktrace shows auth issuer mismatch for EU tokens.
Jun: Digging into the routing logs now. I see the route table TTL refresh failed at 09:10 and fallback policy allowed cross-region routing.
Priya: Confirmed — the routing agent retried against a cached route that listed us-central. We have traces where kv-cache prefix was valid but region tag was missing.
Miguel: Any idea why TTL refresh failed? cloud-dns API errors?
Jun: The control-plane call to zone-sync returned 504 from the provider for ~40s which coincided with our route refresh window. Fallback kicked in per policy.
Aisha: Support: are these customers seeing billing anomalies or partial failures (like embeddings ok but generation fails)?
Tom: Most report generation latency and intermittent 5xx from /v1/generate. Embeddings and simple key checks generally succeed when routed to correct region. But customers that hit the wrong region saw a mix of 401 and 503.
support-bot: Customer: acme-inc — reported at 09:15 UTC: "API error 401 and huge latency" — ticket #3412 created.
Priya: Repro steps I used: set X-Region: eu-west header disabled in client, force refresh window, then simulate zone-sync timeout. Routing decision reverted to fallback agent -> us-central.
Jun: Here's the quick repro command we used: 
```
# simulate control-plane delay
curl -X POST https://internal-control/zone-sync/simulate?delay=45 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
# then send requests to regional endpoint
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <eu-token>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Aisha: Root cause (short) — zone-sync refresh timed out causing route metadata to be stale; fallback policy allowed cross-region failover which triggered auth audience mismatches and higher latency.
Tom: Mitigations we applied during incident: 1) tightened fallback policy at 09:22 to require same-region auth verification, 2) force-refreshed route table at 09:24, 3) rolled a small hotfix to the routing agent to prefer region affinity while control-plane is degraded at 09:30.
Miguel: Did we notify affected customers and provide workaround?
Tom: Yes — support sent an interim reply with workaround: set region header to eu-west or use dedicated endpoint; ticket updates at 09:28.
Priya: Postmortem notes I'm drafting: timeline, root cause, blast radius, repro steps, and action items (short/medium/long term).
Aisha: Action items (assigned): 
• Jun: Add exponential backoff + jitter to zone-sync and surface metrics for refresh failures. (ETA 1w)
• Priya: Update routing runbook to include immediate fix steps and customer-facing wording. (ETA 2d)
• Miguel (support): Send follow-up to all impacted customers with SLA credit info and confirm billing unaffected. (ETA 1d)
• Tom: Add alert when cross-region failover rate > 0.5% in 5m window and include auth mismatch count. (ETA 3d)
• Eng (oncall): Short-term config change to require region affinity for fallback (merged 09:30) — will be reverted to smarter policy after testing.
Aisha: Postmortem draft link: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/1763401234-region-routing-failover-draft — please review.
Jun: Notes: need tests to cover route metadata loss -> fallback behavior. I can add integration test that simulates zone-sync timeout.
Priya: Also add a playbook step to verify token audience when routing changes — prevents silent 401s.
Tom: Lessons learned: fallback policies need to be conservative on auth-sensitive routes; control-plane flakiness should surface faster.
Aisha: Closing notes: no billing data lost, but customer latency/availability impacted for ~18 minutes (09:12–09:30 UTC). We'll follow up with formal postmortem and customer comms. :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Ticket 3412 marked as incident-affected; customer follow-up scheduled.
deploy-bot: config-change (routing-fallback): merged by tom at 09:30, deployed to prod at 09:31.
